pr.title: fix: properly hydrate dynamic css props components and remove element removal

testCase.title: Nested dynamic component keeps its scoped CSS custom property after re-render
testCase.preconditions: A page renders an outer component chosen dynamically (bound to a component variable, not a static tag name); that outer component itself renders an inner component that is also dynamically selected, and the inner component receives a CSS custom property (e.g. --prop) consumed by its own scoped stylesheet.
steps: Load the page and note the color of the text rendered by the inner component.
Click the control that reassigns the outer binding to a different dynamically-selected component.
Observe the color of the text rendered by the newly-selected inner component.
testCase.expectedResult: The inner component's text renders in the color driven by the CSS custom property (red) both before and after the toggle, and no runtime or hydration error occurs.

metadata.feature: compiler / dynamic component rendering with scoped CSS props

provenance.note: PR #16118 (merged 2025-06-11) reworked how dynamic <Component> tags are compiled, including nested dynamic components using scoped CSS custom properties. Issue #16163, filed against a version built on top of #16118, reports 'Rendering a dynamic component within a dynamic component is broken'. PR #16185 (merged 2025-06-17), titled 'fix: avoid shadowing a variable in dynamic components', states in its description: 'Fixes #16163 caused by regression in #16118', and adds the regression test packages/svelte/tests/runtime-browser/samples/css-props-dynamic-component/_config.js which asserts the inner component keeps rgb(255,0,0) text color both before and after toggling the outer dynamic binding.

testCase.title: Multi-line new URL(asset, import.meta.url) reference is bundled as a static asset
testCase.preconditions: A source module references an asset (e.g. a worker script) using new URL(...) with import.meta.url as the second argument, where the call is split across multiple lines for readability.
steps:
Add a module containing a multi-line reference such as:
new URL(
  './worker.js',
  import.meta.url
)
Run a production build.
Inspect the generated output directory and the emitted JavaScript for the module.
testCase.expectedResult: The referenced asset file is emitted into the build output (e.g. under assets/), and the generated code resolves the URL to that emitted file at runtime, identically to how a single-line new URL(...) reference would be handled.

metadata.feature: production asset bundling for new URL(..., import.meta.url)

provenance.note: PR #20358 (merged 2025-07-25) switched assetImportMetaUrlPlugin's transform hook to rolldown's filter-based API, replacing the unconditional string-includes gate with a `code: /new\s+URL.+import\.meta\.url/` filter regex whose `.` does not match newlines by default. Issue #20631 (filed with vite 7.1.x, which contains #20358) reports that a pdfjs-dist worker asset referenced via multi-line new URL(...) is no longer bundled. PR #20644 ('fix: support multiline new URL(..., import.meta.url) expressions', merged 2025-08-19) states verbatim: 'This regression was introduced in #20358 when hook filters were added to internal plugins,' identifies the exact same regex as the cause, adds the `s` (dotAll) flag, and adds an E2E test file for multiline expressions under playground/assets.

Close #4802

testCase.title: Preview command runs for items containing a NUL byte when using a NUL field delimiter
testCase.preconditions: fzf is invoked with a NUL byte as the field delimiter (--delimiter=$'\0'), a common way to encode multiple fields per input line, and a --preview command is configured.
steps: Pipe NUL-delimited input into fzf, e.g.: printf '\0foo\0/\n' | fzf --delimiter=$'\0' --preview 'echo ok'
Observe the preview window for the highlighted item.
testCase.expectedResult: The preview window runs the configured command and shows its output ("ok"); fzf stays usable and does not report an error about the child process failing to start.

provenance.note: PR #4803 (merged 2026-05-23, released in 0.73.0) added FZF_CURRENT_ITEM to the child-process environment by appending the raw current item text unconditionally. pr.title: [Android] Use EdgeToEdge.enable/WindowCompat for edge-to-edge mode instead of deprecated View flags
pr.description:
## Summary

Replaces deprecated `View.SYSTEM_UI_FLAG_LAYOUT_*` flags and `setSystemUiVisibility()` with modern AndroidX APIs for edge-to-edge mode in `PlatformPlugin`.

- For `ComponentActivity` instances (e.g. `FlutterFragmentActivity`), uses `EdgeToEdge.enable()` which also suppresses Android 15 edge-to-edge warnings
- For plain `Activity` instances (e.g. `FlutterActivity`), falls back to `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows()` which achieves the same layout behavior
- Tracks edge-to-edge state to prevent `setSystemUiVisibility()` from interfering with `WindowCompat` on API < 30
- Properly restores normal inset behavior when switching away from edge-to-edge mode

Other system UI modes (lean back, immersive, immersive sticky) are left unchanged as they are lower priority per [issue comment](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/165328#issuecomment-2730332785) — those modes are ignored on API 36+ anyway.

Fixes https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/165328

## Test plan

- Updated existing `setSystemUiMode` test to remove deprecated EDGE_TO_EDGE flag verification
- Updated `doNotEnableEdgeToEdgeOnOlderSdk` test to also verify `WindowCompat` is not called on API < 29
- Added `setSystemUiMode_edgeToEdge_usesWindowCompat` test verifying `WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(window, false)` is called for plain Activity
- Added `switchFromEdgeToEdgeToImmersive_restoresDecorFitsSystemWindows` test verifying mode switching restores `setDecorFitsSystemWindows(true)` then applies immersive flags
- Added `updateSystemUiOverlays_inEdgeToEdge_reappliesModernApi` test verifying overlay restore re-applies `WindowCompat` instead of deprecated `setSystemUiVisibility`

testCase.title: Switching Android system UI mode from immersiveSticky back to edgeToEdge restores the system bars
testCase.preconditions: A Flutter app is running on an Android device or emulator with edge-to-edge support (API 29+).
steps: Call SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.immersiveSticky) to hide the status bar and navigation bar.
Call SystemChrome.setEnabledSystemUIMode(SystemUiMode.edgeToEdge).
Observe the status bar and navigation bar.
testCase.expectedResult: The status bar and navigation bar reappear (system bars are shown) after switching to edgeToEdge mode.

provenance.note: PR #183072 (merged 2026-04-02, in Flutter 3.44.0) replaced deprecated View.SYSTEM_UI_FLAG_* handling with WindowCompat/EdgeToEdge APIs in PlatformPlugin.java for edge-to-edge mode. Issue #186723 ('[Regression][Android] Failed to switch SystemUIMode from immersiveSticky to edgeToEdge in Flutter 3.44.0') was bisected by a reporter to PR #183072; maintainer camsim99 confirmed: 'I can confirm that this is a regression caused by https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/183072. The problem is that calls to set system UI flags for non-edge-to-edge SystemUIModes conflict with the call to Window.setDecorFitsSystemWindows to set edge-to-edge mode.' Maintainer dbebawy then stated 'The fix landed in #187207 (merged to master 2026-05-28)', which corrects the interaction between the legacy setSystemUiVisibility path and the new WindowCompat-based edge-to-edge path added by #183072.

pr.title: fix(tui): late-arriving OSC11 response triggers OptionSet
pr.diff:
diff --git a/runtime/lua/vim/_core/defaults.lua b/runtime/lua/vim/_core/defaults.lua
index 88f41c82d3c9a1..e1776ecf051d77 100644
--- a/runtime/lua/vim/_core/defaults.lua
+++ b/runtime/lua/vim/_core/defaults.lua
@@ -921,7 +921,8 @@ do
           if rr and gg and bb then
             local luminance = (0.299 * rr) + (0.587 * gg) + (0.114 * bb)
             local bg = luminance < 0.5 and 'dark' or 'light'
-            vim.api.nvim_set_option_value('background', bg, {})
+            -- Use :noautocmd to suppress OptionSet event; OSC11 response may arrive after VimEnter.
+            vim.cmd('noautocmd set background=' .. bg)
           end
         end
       end)

testCase.title: Terminal background color change after startup fires OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands
testCase.preconditions: Neovim is started in a terminal that reports background color via the OSC 11 escape sequence (e.g. a terminal that tracks the OS light/dark appearance), and the user has registered autocommands on the OptionSet event (pattern 'background') and on the ColorScheme event.
steps: Start Neovim in a terminal that supports OSC 11 background color notifications and let it finish starting.
Add autocommands: an OptionSet autocommand for pattern 'background', and a ColorScheme autocommand, each printing a message when triggered.
Change the terminal's color mode (e.g. switch the terminal or OS from dark to light) so the terminal emits an updated OSC 11 background response.
testCase.expectedResult: Neovim updates the 'background' option to match the new terminal color mode and both the OptionSet and ColorScheme autocommands fire.

provenance.note: PR #40270 (merged 2026-06-15) changed the automatic background-detection code in runtime/lua/vim/_core/defaults.lua from `vim.api.nvim_set_option_value('background', bg, {})` to `vim.cmd('noautocmd set background=' .. bg)`, to stop a late-arriving startup OSC11 response from firing OptionSet during startup. This unconditionally suppressed autocmd events for every future automatic background update, not only the startup one. Issue #41146 ('No events are emitted on background change caused by OSC signal') reports that OptionSet/ColorScheme no longer fire when the terminal's color mode changes after startup. Maintainer zeertzjq wrote: 'I think this is a regression from #40270 ... Perhaps #40270 should be reverted' and then 'So basically #40270 should be reverted.' PR #41242 ('fix(defaults): emit events on automatic background change', merged 2026-08-10) states 'After #40270, events are no longer emitted from the automatic background detection... BG change after startup still triggers autocmds #41146' and closes #41146.

pr.title: [syntax-errors] Multiple assignments in `case` pattern
pr.description:
Summary
--

This PR detects multiple assignments to the same name in `case` patterns by recursively visiting each pattern.

Test Plan
--

New inline tests.

(Diff shown below excludes two generated parser snapshot files under crates/ruff_python_parser/tests/snapshots/; the full PR also updated those snapshots to match the new diagnostics.)

testCase.title: A case pattern binding a class keyword to a variable of the same name reports no syntax error
testCase.preconditions: A Python 3.10+ file contains a match statement with a case clause matching a class pattern whose keyword argument name equals the variable it binds to (e.g. case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):), and the checker is run with preview mode enabled.
steps:
Run the checker with preview mode enabled (ruff check --preview) on a file containing a match statement such as:
match feature_type:
    case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):
        return num_classes
    case _:
        raise TypeError
Inspect the reported diagnostics for that file.
testCase.expectedResult: No syntax error is reported for the case pattern; the file passes the check cleanly, since a class-pattern keyword name matching the name it binds to is valid, unambiguous Python syntax.

metadata.feature: preview syntax-error detection for match/case patterns

provenance.note: PR #16957 (merged 2025-03-26, shipped as a preview feature in ruff 0.11.3 per the 0.11.3 release notes) added a MatchClass-pattern check that inserts each keyword's attribute name (e.g. `num_classes` in `num_classes=num_classes`) into the same 'seen names' set used for bound variables, so a keyword whose attribute name equals its bound variable name is wrongly flagged as a duplicate binding. Issue #17181 ('Regression: multiple assignments in match statement') and duplicate #17193 ('Regression 0.11.2 -> 0.11.3: SyntaxError on match statement') report this false positive. Verified directly: `pip install ruff==0.11.2` and `ruff check --preview --target-version py310` on `case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):` passes cleanly, while the identical command with `ruff==0.11.3` reports 'SyntaxError: multiple assignments to name `num_classes` in pattern'. PR #17184 ('[syntax-errors] Fix multiple assignment for class keyword argument', merged 2025-04-03) states 'Fixes #17181' and explains the keyword-vs-binding conflation is the cause.

testCase.title: A case pattern binding a class keyword to a variable of the same name reports no syntax error
testCase.preconditions: A Python 3.10+ file contains a match statement with a case clause matching a class pattern whose keyword argument name equals the variable it binds to (e.g. case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):), and the checker is run with preview mode enabled.
steps:
Run the checker with preview mode enabled (ruff check --preview) on a file containing a match statement such as:
match feature_type:
    case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):
        return num_classes
    case _:
        raise TypeError
Inspect the reported diagnostics for that file.
testCase.expectedResult: No syntax error is reported for the case pattern; the file passes the check cleanly, since a class-pattern keyword name matching the name it binds to is valid, unambiguous Python syntax.

metadata.feature: preview syntax-error detection for match/case patterns

provenance.note: PR #16957 (merged 2025-03-26, shipped as a preview feature in ruff 0.11.3 per the 0.11.3 release notes) added a MatchClass-pattern check that inserts each keyword's attribute name (e.g. `num_classes` in `num_classes=num_classes`) into the same 'seen names' set used for bound variables, so a keyword whose attribute name equals its bound variable name is wrongly flagged as a duplicate binding. Issue #17181 ('Regression: multiple assignments in match statement') and duplicate #17193 ('Regression 0.11.2 -> 0.11.3: SyntaxError on match statement') report this false positive. Verified directly: `pip install ruff==0.11.2` and `ruff check --preview --target-version py310` on `case ClassLabel(num_classes=num_classes):` passes cleanly, while the identical command with `ruff==0.11.3` reports 'SyntaxError: multiple assignments to name `num_classes` in pattern'. PR #17184 ('[syntax-errors] Fix multiple assignment for class keyword argument', merged 2025-04-03) states 'Fixes #17181' and explains the keyword-vs-binding conflation is the cause.
